thesisQuality.note: Essential regulated service, 8.7M electric customers, modernization and large-load framework support durable demand; regulatory economics cap the score below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Capital access and operating scale support execution, but equity-unit financing and capital intensity create meaningful funding/dilution pressure.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: At $117.53 with 17.70x trailing and 16.42x forward P/E, valuation is broadly balanced with plausible upside but not rare asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Large-load contracting, grid/storage investment and cost-saving initiatives are source-supported multi-year catalysts, tempered by regulatory timing.

governancePower.note: Management is executing financing, utility combination/cost initiatives and customer-protection structures; capital intensity and dilution prevent an exceptional assessment.

alignment2036.note: Reliable electricity, grid modernization, storage and growing industrial/data-center loads are foundational long-duration infrastructure needs across plausible 2036 futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Multiple regulated electric jurisdictions plus gas utilities and reusable grid/generation capabilities provide several demand channels, though regulated geography remains concentrated in the U.S.

bottleneckControl.note: Duke controls regulated grid/generation capacity in service territories with long infrastructure lead times, but regulators and alternative generation constrain unilateral bottleneck power.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified generation/storage and essential demand support several scenarios, while rate recovery, financing cost and large-load forecast error remain material concentrations.

substitutionResilience.note: Regulated network assets and generation/storage portfolios have high replacement friction; technology mix can adapt, though distributed alternatives and regulatory choices remain substitutes at the margin.

supplyChainResilience.note: Generation diversification and utility scale provide some resilience, but current lineage does not establish exceptional supplier redundancy and major capital projects retain long-lead dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Regulated recovery and large-load customer protections preserve economics better than commodity pricing, but rates remain commission-governed rather than discretionary.

risk.note: Moderate risk reflects regulatory recovery, capital intensity, equity-linked dilution and load-forecast error; essential regulated demand mitigates but does not remove these exposures.

confidence.note: Identity and tradability are validated; multiple fresh primary origins plus independent current valuation data support all components, while some issuer claims lack independent operational corroboration and jurisdiction sensitivity is unquantified.

thesis: Duke is a regulated electricity-infrastructure platform positioned to monetize durable grid modernization and large-load growth, with essential-service resilience offset by regulatory and financing constraints.
keyRisk: Capital intensity and regulatory recovery can convert strong load growth into dilution or weak per-share economics if forecasts, approvals or financing assumptions disappoint.
nextCatalyst: Execution of large-load contracts, grid/storage buildout and customer-cost initiatives through the next regulatory and earnings updates.
